Cross-platform winning patterns (what the top performers share)

  1. Bold condensed CAPS display type is universal (Bebas / Archivo Black / Anton). Our Anton choice was right - the typeface was never the problem.
  2. High value-contrast + brightness stops the scroll (cited +29-32% CTR). A dark scrim over a dim photo (v1) reads as a muddy rectangle - the #1 fix was to lighten.
  3. The photo must match the promise and be bright - real working room or a clean graphic poster.
  4. Date / time / place / price stated flatly + prominently on the image, not buried.
  5. One reframe / pattern-interrupt hook (7 words max on the image).
  6. WHO-callout on the creative ("Utah business owners") - in Meta's Andromeda era, creative IS the targeting.
  7. Price anchor + specific scarcity ($47 was $97; "small group, limited seats").
  8. CTA = "Sign Up" for events (beats "Learn More" by up to 40%).

Full synthesis + all 13 screenshots saved at output/workshop/ads/research/.

3. The four final creatives

1080x1080, text composited in HTML/CSS with real Anton + Archivo (rendered crisp via headless browser - never baked into the AI image). Bright candid photos generated as representative scenes. Truth-only: the June 25 run had 0 attendees, so no creative implies past attendance or shows fake numbers.

A - REFRAME. "This is not a seminar. It's a working session." Pattern-interrupt. Council: secondary split-test.

B - PAIN. "Everyone says use AI. Nobody shows you how." The photo IS someone being shown how.

C - BUILD. "Build one AI thing you actually use." Council: PRIMARY. Bring the task, we build the fix, you keep it.

D - CLEAN POSTER (new). "Walk in unsure. Walk out using it." Bright orange Anik-Singal model. Brightest + highest contrast.

  • C = primary (keep). Council asked for a local-grounding element -> added "SLCC Miller Campus · small group, limited seats" to all four.
  • A = secondary split-test (keep). "NOT A SEMINAR" pattern-interrupt validated.
  • B = keep. Closure supplied by the venue/scarcity line + subhead resolution.
  • D: council leaned kill ("identity theater"). Fixed instead by naming the concrete deliverable in D's subhead ("One real tool, built for your business, in 90 minutes") - grounded scaffolding, not theater. Kept as the brightest variant.

Open question the council raised, your call: name the ONE concrete tool every attendee leaves with. That single decision would sharpen every creative's believability further.

CTA in Ads Manager: Sign Up. Anti-patterns refused: no fabricated proof, no fake headcount/testimonial, no implied past attendance, no refund/guarantee, no em-dashes.

The locked walk-out deliverable: The Daily Three

You locked it: every attendee leaves with three AI tools they set up live in the room and use every day. Plain-language names, zero jargon. This is now on the primary creatives and woven into the workshop, seat, and checklist pages.

The 5-Angle Pressure-Test

Make AI argue against your decision from five expert angles before you commit. You catch the hole while it is still cheap to fix.

The Pre-Mortem

Have AI tell you why your plan fails before you spend the money. You walk in with the failure mapped, so you spend on what moves it.

The Plain-Answer Filter

Stop AI from overcomplicating. You get back the clean, usable answer you can act on, not a wall of options.

Headline value line now on creatives A, C, D: "Leave with 3 AI tools you will use every day." B keeps its pain-led angle per the council split. Truth held: 0 prior attendees, so no testimonial, no headcount, no implied past attendance.
